questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In an experiment testing if screen time affects sleep hours, keeping bedtime routine the same, what is the independent variable?
questions.why: The independent variable is the one the experimenter deliberately changes — here, screen time. Sleep hours is what's measured (dependent), and bedtime routine is kept the same (controlled).

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Act 1 Scene 1, who tries to stop the servants' street fight?
questions.why: Benvolio, Romeo's peace-loving cousin, tries to break up the servants' brawl by drawing his sword only to part them. Tybalt instead arrives to fuel the fight, showing the contrast between the two characters.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In the four-chord song C–Am–F–G, which chord is played last?
questions.why: The order C, Am, F, G puts G in the final spot, matching the 'V' position in I–vi–IV–V. Students often assume the progression ends back on the home chord (C), but it actually ends on G before looping round.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these ranks in Japan's feudal hierarchy
questions.why: The emperor stayed at the top in name, but the shogun held real power, ruling over daimyo (regional lords), who in turn commanded samurai warriors.

questions.subject: Japanese
questions.prompt: How do you say 'please give me this' when ordering food in Japanese?
questions.why: 'Kudasai' means 'please give me' and is used when ordering. 'Oishii' means delicious, 'itadakimasu' is said before eating, and 'gochisousama' is said after.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: The chance of a spinner landing on purple is 0.45. What is the chance it does not land on purple?
questions.why: Complementary events add to 1, so the chance of not landing on purple is 1 − 0.45 = 0.55.
